source.title: Empirical Guidelines for Deploying LLMs onto Resource-constrained Edge Devices
source.authors: Ruiyang Qin; Dan-Cheng Liu; Chen-Hui Xu; Zheyu Yan; Zhao-Xuan Tan; Zhenge Jia; Amir Nassereldine; Jia-Jie Li; Meng Jiang; Ahmed Abbasi; Jin-Jun Xiong; Yi-Yu Shi

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; some figure content is not numerically recoverable from the text extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream task scores across model sizes, bearing on the scale-related part of V6, but it does not measure pretraining cross-entropy or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and discusses a cited pre-power-law account of fine-tuning, but it reports no held-out pretraining-loss measurements, parameter/token/compute scaling-law fits, small-run extrapolations, or compute-optimal parameter-token allocation. Its fine-tuning-duration and RAG-data results use downstream task metrics rather than loss, so they do not test V1–V5 or V7. Figure 2 compares task scores across model sizes and is included for V6; plotted values are not numerically recoverable here.
record.test_reason: The paper is not a scaling-law study, but it reports downstream scores across model sizes in a new setting: edge customization on the personalized LaMP tasks. These include zero-shot and fine-tuned scores for the Pythia and OPT size suites (Tables 7–8). This bears on V6's scale part. It measures no pretraining loss and fits no scaling law, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. T3 fits better than the reader's T2, since the study does not aim at the scaling question.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the best edge model and customization method depend on task difficulty. They find that the largest trainable parameters and longest fine-tuning are not optimal, and that compressed models sometimes beat uncompressed ones. They also state that a larger model is not always better, though bigger models help on summarization. They frame this as filling a gap in scaling laws for resource-constrained settings, without testing those laws.
record.recipe_differences: Studies edge deployment and downstream task metrics under customization and resource constraints, rather than fitting held-out pretraining loss against model size, data, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported preferred model and customization method vary with downstream task difficulty.

fits_no_version.finding: Longer LoRA fine-tuning (more user samples) does not monotonically improve downstream scores, and more RAG history data (100→1000 samples) adds little.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream gains from small-scale personalized fine-tuning or retrieval data do not follow a clean scaling trend at 10^2–10^3 samples.

record.problems: Figure 2 values are figure-only in the extracted text; the paper compares different model families and sizes, so the comparisons do not isolate parameter count as a cause. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were extracted from the extensive fine-tuning, RAG, or compression experiments: they report downstream task performance or resource outcomes, not the pretraining-loss behavior in V1–V5 or the fitting-dependence claim in V7.

untested.parts: Prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss; any fitted predictive relation; scale beyond 13B; standard benchmarks.
All: no held-out pretraining loss is measured.
All: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
All: fine-tuning outcomes are downstream metrics, not loss power laws.

missing.what: Zero-shot scores per size for the Pythia and OPT suites on LaMP-1 to LaMP-7; these are the cleanest size comparison in the paper.
Fine-tuned (rank 8, alpha 16, 8h) and RAG scores per size for the Pythia and OPT suites and other models.
Gemma-2b-GPTQ vs Gemma-7b-GPTQ across LoRA settings and training hours.
Within-family size × training-time comparisons for Pythia and OPT, and for the quantized Llama 1b–13b models.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is weak for V6. The data are 100 users per task with no uncertainty reported, families and quantization are mixed, and fine-tuning is time-matched so larger models see fewer samples. The verdicts rest on the appendix tables rather than the figure-only rows.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured against parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
No scaling-law fit from small runs or prediction of larger-run loss is reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or fitted parameter/token trends are reported.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
The study evaluates downstream task scores during customization, not whether held-out loss follows the same power-law form in fine-tuning or other regimes.
Tests model-size comparisons on selected downstream tasks, but not prediction from pretraining loss or a fitted predictive relationship across tasks.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared across setup or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot, within the Pythia (70m–2.8b) and OPT (125m–2.7b) suites on LaMP tasks
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Table 8), not on the rows. Scores are non-monotonic in size: Pythia LaMP-2 goes 0.230/0.310/0.240/0.130 (410m→2.8b), OPT LaMP-2 goes 0.031/0.210/0.035/0.150, and Pythia LaMP-4 is flat at about 0.03. Only the jump from zero at 70m–160m is consistent.
relationships.display_finding: In zero-shot evaluation, Pythia LaMP-2 scores varied 0.230/0.310/0.240/0.130 and OPT scores 0.031/0.210/0.035/0.150, while Pythia LaMP-4 stayed near 0.03; only the increase from zero at 70m–160m was consistent.

relationships.condition: LoRA fine-tuning under a fixed time budget (larger models see fewer samples), within families
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Tables 7 and 9). Pythia FT on LaMP-1 goes 0.275/0.039/0.559/0.500, and on LaMP-2 it saturates around 0.46–0.475. Gemma-7b-GPTQ falls far below 2b on LaMP-7 (0.030 vs 0.227). Size and data budget are confounded.
relationships.display_finding: Pythia LaMP-1 scores varied 0.275/0.039/0.559/0.500 and LaMP-2 saturated around 0.46–0.475, while Gemma-7b-GPTQ scored 0.030 versus 0.227 for 2b on LaMP-7; larger models saw fewer samples.
